workflows.name: Contractor Delivery Cost per Order Analytics

Automation Opportunity: - Pricing auto-computed from the cost + margin target; settlement auto-reconciled with discrepancy-flagging; invoice auto-generated from the POD/delivery record
Controls: - CTL-453 (ensure controlled execution — Job Site Delivery Performance & Analytics (PA-74.3).)
- operational: Finance Analyst sign-off on the workflow output
Pain Points / Risks: - **Margin-erosion risk**: pricing miscalculation (commission, discount, surcharge) erodes net margin below target; mitigated by the margin-floor guard and pre-launch validation

- **Data-quality risk**: incomplete or inaccurate master data (pricing, inventory, customer) corrupts the workflow output; mitigated by the master-data governance (VS-29 / W291) and the periodic audit
System Touchpoints: - Order management (links to VS-08 / W536 unified order management, VS-60 / W2286 routing)
- Pricing/financials (links to VS-17 / W9 financial close, VS-29 / W289 pricing master)
- Logistics/DC (links to VS-04 / W3 receiving, VS-04 / W52 fleet, VS-77 / material staging)
Time Estimate: - ~2–3 days per occurrence (per the step durations)
- Absorbed into the Finance Analyst role; not incremental headcount unless volume scales significantly.

steps.activity: Finance Analyst calculates delivery cost per contractor order: direct costs (fuel, driver, 3PL), indirect costs, special equipment surcharges; compares against fee charged
Analyst identifies cost optimization: consolidate routes, negotiate better 3PL rates, reduce crane frequency, encourage self-pickup for smaller orders
Finance Controller reviews contractor delivery profitability: revenue vs. cost; identifies money-losing routes; proposes fee adjustments or minimum orders for free delivery
